stories.headline: Fabian Hürzeler commits to Brighton following Man United rumours
stories.summary: Fabian Hürzeler has confirmed his commitment to Brighton after receiving strong backing from Seagulls chief Tony Bloom.
stories.body:
Fabian Hürzeler has confirmed his commitment to Brighton after receiving strong backing from Seagulls chief Tony Bloom.

Bloom said this week he would fight "ridiculously hard" to keep hold of Hürzeler following reports that Manchester United had considered him as a potential replacement for sacked boss Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino was appointed as the United head coach last week.

Hürzeler is getting rave reviews for his work on the south coast and is preparing for his side's trip to Hull on Sunday sitting second in the Premier League table.

Hürzeler told a press conference: "I've spoken a lot about his [Bloom's] support, trust and belief.

"It's a privilege to work here and since my time here there's been a lot of rumours with other clubs, but they are just rumours and I am fully committed to this club."

The Seagulls have mixed injury news with the likes of Chema Andrés and Yankuba Minteh available and Stefanos Tzimas and Kaoru Mitoma nearing returns to fitness, but Zadok Yohanna is out after a setback on international duty.

- Drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino at Man United apologises

- Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season

- Reranking the MVP for each of the top Premier League clubs

Hürzeler warned Hull will be no pushovers after their impressive return to the top flight and the tough test they gave leaders Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium two weeks ago.

He added: "They are doing an impressive job. They are very structured. Arsenal suffered so we need to be patient.

"We know they are good in transition and have individual quality, as well as set-pieces. I don't think it's an easy place to go."

stories.headline: Lance Broadway, ex-White Sox, Mets pitcher who turned to acting, dies at 43
stories.summary: Lance Broadway, a former MLB first-round pick who became an actor following his baseball career, has died. He was 43.
stories.body:
DALLAS -- Lance Broadway, a major league pitcher who became an actor following his baseball career, has died. He was 43.

His cause of death was not immediately clear. The report posted Thursday by the Dallas County Medical Examiner's Office said Broadway died Tuesday in a stairwell at an apartment complex near Love Field Airport.

Dallas Police did not immediately respond to an open records request for reports involving Broadway's death.

Broadway pitched in college at Dallas Baptist and TCU. He was taken in the first round of the 2005 draft by the Chicago White Sox and appeared in a total of 27 games for them and the New York Mets from 2007 to 2009.

He made his movie debut in "Olympus Has Fallen" in 2013 and appeared in several television series.

stories.headline: Windhorst and MacMahon: League execs, scouts examine nine rookie starts
stories.summary: How has the first month unfolded for nine first-year stars? Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon canvass the league.
stories.body:
For NBA front offices, the first two months of the season are defined by evaluation -- what your team has, what it needs and the priorities of 29 other teams.

At the forefront is watching the league's rookies.

"You assess the situation they're in and then you assess their play," a Western Conference executive said. "Not all situations are created equal, and you can't judge the young guys all equally."

That is happening in earnest with the vaunted 2026 draft class. Here is a look at what the experts are seeing so far.

Jump to rookie intel:

Dybantsa | Peterson | Boozer

Wilson | Wagler | Brown | Acuff

Flemings | Lendeborg

1. AJ Dybantsa, Washington Wizards
2026-27: 16.3 PTS | 6.6 REB | 2.3 AST | 41.6 FG%

Brian Windhorst: A few rookies are shooting well, but when discussing players in their first NBA season, frequently you will see them struggling with efficiency. So getting this feedback on the Wizards' No. 1 pick, who had his best scoring game of the season Wednesday against the Toronto Raptors, is somewhat typical.

Having said that, opinions of his situation spanned beyond his 21% mark on 3s so far.

"He's in a tough environment for a rookie," an Eastern Conference scout told ESPN. "There's not a high level of accountability there for their top players and so there isn't down the line."

"He's so big, so powerful and plays so much force that it demands that he have the ball and space," a West executive said. "But it's hard with [Anthony Davis and Trae Young] there because they are soaking up a lot of the possessions and the team is naturally going to cater to them."

Dybantsa, who had a late start because of an ankle injury, is warming up. He has averaged 17 points over the past three games and had a season-best 23 in Toronto on Wednesday as the Wizards broke their eight-game losing streak.

2. Darryn Peterson, Utah Jazz

2026-27: 16.5 PTS | 4.1 REB | 3.6 AST | 40.4 FG%

Windhorst: Earlier this month, Peterson had a five-game run of 20-plus points with 17 total 3-pointers, which definitely got everyone excited. Eyebrows were raised higher when he asked to come out of a game last week with a knee issue, which called to mind events last year at Kansas. Peterson bounced back in the next game and has played every night.

"I think he looks good. He hasn't been very efficient yet, but they're letting him go," a West scout said. "He's just so talented, he'll need some patience."

The Jazz got a couple of much-needed wins this week, relieving some pressure. This is where "situation" comes into play.

"I've seen [Peterson] in person a few times already and he's awesome, but he's a 2-guard, he's not a PG," a West executive said. "They don't really have a true point guard; they have two scoring guards [Peterson and Keyonte George] who they are trying to play at point guard and it's giving them some issues."

3. Cameron Boozer, Memphis Grizzlies
2026-27: 16.6 PTS | 9.2 REB | 5.3 AST | 41.7 FG%

Tim MacMahon: Several teams, especially those leaning into analytics in their evaluations, had the Grizzlies power forward as the top player on their board.

"I don't think he had the highest ceiling," a West coach, who considered Boozer the best prospect in the draft, said. "It's just that you were never going to look back 10 years from now and be mad that you picked him."

Boozer already processes the game at an elite level, allowing him to average 5.3 assists as a rookie. He inherited the muscular frame and nose for the ball from his father, former All-Star power forward Carlos Boozer, as evidenced by the 19-year-old leading all rookies with 9.4 rebounds per game.

Boozer has immediately impacted winning in Memphis, logging the most minutes for a young Grizzlies squad that has a case for the league's most pleasant surprise with an 11-4 record.

But some scouts and executives are skeptical about his superstar potential. Boozer measured at 6-foot-8¼ without shoes and lacks explosiveness, leading to questions about his ability to finish against NBA big men. His field goal percentage (40.0%) is the blemish on an otherwise impressive stat line. "He plays below the rim on both ends of the floor," a West scout said.

Windhorst: The Grizzlies are off to an excellent start, and some weren't surprised when they won in Washington against Dybantsa this week.

"Boozer kicked [his draft class'] asses in almost every AAU game from ninth to 12th grade," an East executive said. "He plays with a ton of confidence, and it didn't just happen yesterday."

"He's got a high IQ," a West scout said. "[The Grizzlies] have a conviction about their players -- they invest and commit to them."

4. Caleb Wilson, Chicago Bulls

2026-27: 18.9 PTS | 6.2 REB | 1.8 STL | 42.0 FG%

Windhorst: The Bulls forward played 10 games before hand surgery disrupted his rookie year, but he has been quite active when on the floor.

"He's uber talented but sometimes he's just running around dunking and shooting 3s," an East executive said. "I don't think he's too focused on passing, but give him some time. He's a very intriguing prospect."

Wilson hoisted 71 3-pointers in 308 minutes before the injury, an aggressive rate for a player who shot under 30% in his one year at North Carolina. He has made just under 33% in the NBA.

"He's an uncut diamond," a West scout said. "High risk and high reward."

MacMahon: One general manager said Wilson wasn't the highest-ranked player on his board, but he believed that he had the potential to emerge as the biggest star in the class.

"I could see Wilson passing [Lendeborg] when he's entering his prime," another executive said, "and Yaxel is 30."

5. Keaton Wagler, LA Clippers

2026-27: 12.1 PTS | 3.4 REB | 3.0 AST | 35.9 3P%

Windhorst: Clippers coach Tyronn Lue is playing Wagler, the No. 5 pick, off the bench behind starting point guard Darius Garland. Lue, who loves Wagler's pick-and-roll instincts, has already admitted there were times when he should've given the rookie more minutes, and that's probably going to be happening.

"He's big, smart and understands the game, sometimes he sees two plays ahead," a West executive said. "His body type and his game, he has [Tyrese] Haliburton written all over him."

The Clippers have been hammered, fairly, for some of their decisions and tactics over the past few seasons. But the deal that sent Ivica Zubac to Indiana, where he's off to an uneven start, for the pick that became Wagler is looking good at the moment.

"Does he have star potential? I'm not sure about that but he's stable and solid," a West scout said. "He doesn't play like a 19-year-old, I'll tell you that. When I saw his age, I actually thought it was off."

6. Mikel Brown Jr., Brooklyn Nets

2026-27: 11.4 PTS | 1.8 REB | 3.8 AST | 34.0 FG%

Windhorst: After Brown's back injury last year at Louisville and an ankle injury in the preseason, the Nets have been bringing the guard along slowly as they build up his body. As such, he hasn't been starting and has been on a pitch count. But his per-36-minute numbers show promise for significant production when he gets to full power.

"He's explosive, and you can play him at both guard positions," an East scout said. "Their situation is not helping, they have a bunch of young guys who are trying to prove they're NBA players."

Brown is regarded as one of the best shooters of the class, though that isn't showing in the games just yet -- he's shooting just 33% on 3s.

"I'm pretty confident in his shooting skill," a West scout said. "If he never does anything else, he can really shoot."

7. Darius Acuff Jr., Sacramento Kings
2026-27: 26.2 PTS | 3.6 REB | 7.0 AST | 41.6 FG%
Windhorst: He's averaging 26 points on 23 shots on a whopping 36.7 minutes a night. The Kings are not a good team, but they are deeply invested in Acuff becoming a star. As such, they're willing to let him shoot through growing pains. Actually, they're letting him shoot through practically everything.

"He plays one way and you have to feature him," an East executive said. "He reminds me of Stephon Marbury, he's strong and he's gonna score that ball. You can win with him, but the team has to be set in a way with a bunch of guys who are comfortable with that. It's hard to find guys like that."

MacMahon: Acuff is the most polarizing player in the class. And the beam-like brightness of Acuff's green light has prompted some grumblings from league observers.

The only players in the league who have hoisted more shots than Acuff this season are two-time scoring champion Luka Doncic and back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

"He needs to realize it's a team game," an East scout said. "There's no doubt he's a talent. Defensively challenged, to say the least. He can pass -- he just doesn't want to pass."

There are concerns about the losing environment in Sacramento, which is 1-13, stunting Acuff's growth.

"He needs to be coached hard and coached well and develop good habits defensively," an East executive said. "It's a shame he's going to waste this year with Doug Christie. But he's going to be a stud offensively for sure."

8. Kingston Flemings, Atlanta Hawks

2026-27: 7.8 PTS | 4.1 AST | 51.4 FG% | 42.9 3P%

Windhorst: Flemings has been slowed by a back injury over the past week but he's already impressed Hawks' coach Quin Snyder, who promoted him to the starting lineup within a month. His minutes will be increasing with veteran CJ McCollum out for at least four weeks with a calf injury, as well.

"He's a two-way player who is pass-first and tough as s---," an East executive said of Flemings. "I was fine with him getting that suspension (for elbowing the Pelicans' Bryce McGowens) as long as he doesn't make a habit of it because it sent a message to the league and his own teammates."

It's early and the volume is low, but the No. 8 pick is an exception to the rule as he's shooting over 50% overall and over 40% on 3s.

"His ceiling will depend on his shooting, it didn't look good in summer league, but he's been better so far," a West scout said. "He gives them youthful energy, he wants to prove himself."

MacMahon: Several opposing scouts and executives have suggested the Hawks could end up regretting passing on Aday Mara with the No. 8 pick, considering the 7-3 big man's instant impact with the Oklahoma City Thunder and Atlanta's lack of size at the center position.

Mara, selected by the Thunder at No. 12 (via the Clippers, of course), worked to improve his physique between summer league and training camp. He had earned a regular role for the Thunder even before injuries thinned Oklahoma City's rotation.

Mara has a 9-foot-9 standing reach -- the second highest measured at the NBA draft combine -- and natural defensive instincts. He's already an outstanding rim protector, averaging 1.7 blocks in 21.9 minutes. Offensively, he's a lob threat with good touch in the paint and a crafty passer.

Another question posed by multiple scouts and executives: Did the Mavs draft the third-best player from coach Dusty May's Michigan title team despite having their pick of the trio? While Lendeborg and Mara are thriving, Morez Johnson Jr. has struggled in a backup center role in Dallas.

Injuries have been a significant issue in Johnson's slow start. He missed much of training camp and the preseason while dealing with shin splints in his right leg and has been bothered recently by a contusion to his left shin. He had a 39-inch maximum vertical leap at the combine, but Johnson hasn't had that same bounce early in his NBA career, reflected in just two blocks across 239 minutes.

11. Yaxel Lendeborg, Golden State Warriors
2026-27: 19.7 PTS | 7.3 REB | 3.7 AST | 37.2 3P%

MacMahon: There was a near consensus among the league's talent evaluators that the top four picks were in a tier of their own, although opinions varied regarding the ranking of that quartet. Lendeborg, who looks like the steal of the draft after going to Golden State at No. 11, has barged into the early Rookie of the Year discussion.

"It's hard to say he can't be the best player in this class," a West executive said of Lendeborg, who ranks second among rookies in scoring (20.3 points) and rebounding (7.3) and sixth in assists (3.5).

The biggest knock on the 6-foot-10, 247-pound Lendeborg was that he turned 24 years old before making his NBA debut. The last lottery pick that old was Chris Duarte, the No. 13 selection in the 2017 draft who averaged 13.1 points as a rookie but was out of the league after four seasons.

"He has to be really good right away or it's a problem," said one West general manager, who had Lendeborg fifth on his board and considered trading into the top 10 to take him, shying away in part due to worries about how the rookie's goofy personality would fit in his team's locker room.

The conventional wisdom was that Lendeborg's potential was much more limited than prospects four or five years younger. But Lendeborg, who didn't begin playing basketball seriously until well into his teens, is disproving that theory. He has continued his trend of improving as a 3-point shooter: 33.3% and 35.7% in his two seasons at Alabama-Birmingham, 37.2% for Michigan's national title team last season and 37.8% from NBA range -- despite a slump since Stephen Curry was injured and Lendeborg became the primary focus of scouting reports.

"I could not have predicted he'd be this good," an East executive said. "His skill at his size is really impressive. Is he a good enough shooter to play [small forward]? I would have said no, but it looks like yes."

Added an East scout: "He's better than expected. He can shoot. He can create his own shot and really handle for his size. A lot of teams are not looking too good [for passing on him]."

stories.headline: Harry Kane sets sights on Champions League, England trophy after Ballon d'Or win
stories.summary: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is on a mission to claim trophies that have so far eluded him in his career, namely a Champions League and a tittle with England.
stories.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is on a mission to claim trophies that have so far eluded him in his career, namely a Champions League crown with Bayern Munich and a tittle with England.

Kane, 33, lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals last season but was rewarded for his stellar campaign at Bayern and his performances with England this summer.

He had 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern and was the Bundesliga's top scorer with 36 goals.

Kane scored six times in seven appearances while captaining England to third place, their best finish at a World Cup since 1966.

Kane, who beat Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to claim football's most prestigious individual award last month, told Footmercato: "Of course, I'd love to win another Ballon d'Or, but I know there are plenty of other great players in with a chance.

"But there are still lots of trophies I'd like to win, such as the Champions League with Bayern and, of course, a title with England."

"I am extremely proud to have won the Ballon d'Or, and receiving this award in my home town [London] made the moment even more special.

"To see my name alongside players such as R9 [Ronaldo Nazario] -- who, incidentally, presented the award to me that evening -- Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Gerd Müller is a source of immense pride, especially given my journey, which included loan spells early in my career that forced me to show self-belief and resilience."

The England captain credits his move to Bayern in the summer of 2023 from Tottenham as pivotal in his career.

"Since joining Bayern, I've clearly taken my game to the next level, and I feel I'm in the best form of my career," he said.

"I think winning the Ballon d'Or has changed the way people perceive me around the world. I'd probably underestimated the excitement and the fans' reaction.

"When I held up the trophy in front of the supporters waiting for me in the street as I left the ceremony, I realised I was experiencing a magical moment that I'll never forget. This victory reflects an exceptional season I've had, filled with goals, titles and memorable moments.

"Winning the Ballon d'Or at the age of 33 simply shows that if you keep working hard and believing in yourself, you can reach the very top."

- Harry Kane: England and Spain are 'the best teams in international football'

- Harry Kane stats: His most eye-opening England cap, goal records

- Kane thanks doctor who reinvigorated his career ahead of record-breaking 126th cap

Kane, who has won two consecutive league titles with Bayern, has his sight set on lifting the Champions League this season. He was close to doing so with Spurs in 2019 but lost 2-0 in the final to Liverpool.

Bayern have not won Europe's elite club competition since 2020 when they beat Paris Saint-Germain in the final, the team that eliminated them last season.

"The Champions League is a major goal for me and for the team," Kane said.

"We've got a strong squad, made up of incredible players. Last season, the matches against PSG were mad -- it was down to the wire -- and being knocked out by the team that won the title twice in a row was nothing to be ashamed of. Spending another year with the manager [Vincent Kompany] and the team is helping us to become even stronger.

"We went into this season telling ourselves that this had to be our year. We need to find a way to make it happen, find that little bit extra that will make the difference to get through the rounds, and do everything we can to win the Champions League. That's our main objective."

The Great One scored 215 points in 1985-86, 212 in '81-82, 208 in '84-85 and 205 in '83-84. Mario Lemieux came closest to Gretzky, finishing the '88-89 season with 199.

Connor McDavid plays for the same Edmonton Oilers franchise that Gretzky did when he posted those totals, and his personal best total is 153, set in 2022-23.

stories.headline: F1 drivers face unique Las Vegas dilemma as GTA VI arrives: Who's playing?
stories.summary: Formula 1's drivers have a unique conundrum this week -- how to dovetail their racing duties at the Las Vegas Grand Prix alongside playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto VI.
stories.body:
Formula 1's drivers have a unique conundrum this week -- how to dovetail their racing duties at the Las Vegas Grand Prix alongside playing the newly-released Grand Theft Auto VI.

Rockstar's sixth instalment of the GTA franchise was release on Nov. 19, right in line with the beginning of the Vegas race schedule.

With 13 years between GTA V and GTA VI, it's been one of the most highly anticipated and hyped games in modern times. Speaking on Thursday night, with half the world already playing it due to the Vegas time zone, Kimi Antonelli admitted he had been bugging friends in Italy for updates.

"I've already downloaded it. I pre-ordered, I did everything. I will ask my dad to bring over the PlayStation," the newly-crowned 2026 world champion told Canadian broadcaster TSN.

"In my free time I will play. Many of us have been waiting for this game and we're all super excited.

"My friends right now are playing it. There's a friend of mine who should be going to work tomorrow. But actually is not going to sleep so he's going to work after playing all night. I've been video calling him all night on WhatsApp, 'how is the game, how is it going?' and everything, he's been showing me.

"It feels like going back 10 years. Feel like a little kid again being so excited for a game. Definitely, I'll be playing, after the weekend in my free time."

Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton has made no secret in recent weeks of his anticipation to play it.

The Ferrari driver suggested he will instead be focusing on preparing properly for the weekend.

"I have my console with me [but] I have the F1 game with me," he said. "That's the one I use on a race weekend because that's the thing that will ultimately help me get the result I ultimately need. I can't wait. I think everyone's been waiting to play it."

Speaking at a fan event later, however, Hamilton admitted GTA is very much on the agenda for this weekend.

"Thursday night I'll be back at the hotel early," he said to loud cheers from the audience. I hope you can tap into the kid you are [when the game is out]."

- Antonelli handed grid penalty for Las Vegas GP; Russell sets pace in FP2

- F1 bosses confirm 'agreement' on V8 engine return deal

- FIA to introduce full-time stewards to address worries over decision-making

The rest of the grid appeared to be working out when they might be able to squeeze in some time on the game around their marketing and racing appearances.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen is famous for racing late into the night on sim racing -- something Red Bull once had to ask him to stop doing, especially when he would do it over race weekends.

"It's already pre-downloaded," the four-time world champion said. "Whenever I have the time I will play. I used to play the previous one also. Of course, my life has changed a little bit compared to then. In a way it's clear the mind sometimes, it's nice and relaxing to do these things."

Verstappen's teammate Isack Hadjar even managed to squeeze in 25 minutes on Thursday, thanks to having with him a PlayStation 5 on a European server.

"I got to play really briefly before having to leave to the track so I'm still on the opening scenes," he said.

Asked by TSN when he will play it during the Vegas race, he laughed and said: "The whole time! Honestly. Hopefully it won't have an impact on my weekend."

Mercedes driver George Russell said: "I did play San Andreas when I was younger. I have been seeing some of the videos and it has given me a bit of the bug. I don't have a console with me. I definitely will give it a whirl."

Drivers should be able to find plenty of downtime to play, especially given the timing of the Vegas race.

The earliest track action begins on Thursday and Friday is 4.30 p.m. local time, and the race itself on Saturday is not until 8 p.m.

F1's Vegas race is followed by a trip to the Middle East, with an event in Qatar on Nov. 29. and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6 to close out the season.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who often plays Call of Duty online against Hamilton, admitted he was kicking himself not to have prepared properly to play in Vegas, although he was already thinking about when he can get his hands on the game.

He said: "I usually bring my laptop. I've left it home -- big mistake! I'll definitely download the game after I get back after the weekend and get on it before Qatar. I love a gaming session, for me it's a nice way to relax."

Williams driver Alex Albon was also regretting his planning, saying: "I was looking into portable [consoles]. If anyone wants to give me one, I'll take it! I think I'll be in my hotel room a fair bit the next few weeks."

McLaren's Lando Norris said that he was banned from playing it growing up and that he would have to reply on his friend's PlayStation.

"I would love to, but I wasn't allowed to play it when I was younger," he said. "I wasn't allowed. So when we would go on a school trip and I could nick someone else's PSP or something, it was the best trip of my life because I could finally get to play it.

"But I never grew up playing it when I was at home. I never really played it when I was older, therefore. So it's never been my thing. But I know a lot of people around the world are playing it right now. So maybe my mind changes. But for now, it's a no."

His teammate Oscar Piastri admitted the craze might have passed him by when he was younger.

"I was far too young for the previous GTA so I've not played before. I don't know," he said. "I don't have any plans [to play] at this point in time. I know there's been a lot of hype around it. If a few people pull my arm then I might have to jump on as well!"

Alpine's Franco Colapinto had no clue the game was out this week.

"Oh, it's out?" he asked when told about it.

"What does it come in? PlayStation? I don't play video games. I thought it had already come out. I saw too many videos, people playing it no?"

When told some people had got their hands on pre-release versions, he laughed and said: "Oh, they were cheating!?" He added: "I don't play video games so much. I was in the simulator since I was very young, so that was like my video game. Not really others.

"I'm quite useless with FIFA [now called EA FC]. When I play with friends I'm not very good at it."

stories.headline: Dike exits wild card loss injured as Orlando's season ends against Cincinnati
stories.summary: FC Cincinnati rallied to eliminate Orlando City 3-1 in MLS Cup Eastern Conference wild card match on Thursday.
stories.body:
Forward Daryl Dike suffered an injury in Orlando City SC's 3-1 defeat to FC Cincinnati in the Major League Soccer playoff wild card match on Thursday night at Inter&Co Stadium in Orlando, Florida.

Dike entered the playoff match in the 75th minute before suffering the injury moments later.

"I don't know what the issue is; we haven't been able to, I haven't had time yet to see the doctors, so I don't know exactly what's wrong," interim coach Martín Perelman said in the post-match press conference.

"I think it's something with his hamstring, since that's where he was holding, so I assume he might have some kind of tear or something similar in the hamstring, but I'm not certain. I don't know exactly what it is, but naturally, he's frustrated, just like the rest of us."

Despite the apparent injury, Dike stayed on the pitch for the rest of the game given that Orlando City did not have any more substitution windows available.

"Regarding the substitutions, these are things that can happen, and they're difficult to predict," Perelman said.

"You never expect a player to come on with 15 minutes left and then get injured; that's not something you anticipate. So, I don't think it's fair to second-guess the substitutions based on that. It simply happened, and that's that-we can't change it now. It was just another piece of misfortune in the match, and, well, as I said, that's part of the game."

Dike has a lengthy injury history, suffering a season-ending hamstring injury in 2022, a right Achilles tendon rupture in 2023, a left Achilles tendon rupture in 2024, and most recently a thigh concern that kept him on the sidelines for 10 matches during the start of the 2025/26 season.

Orlando striker Martín Ojeda opened up the scoring in the 26th minute of the match before goals by Cincinnati players Evander and Samuel Gidi won the game for the visiting side.

Orlando City, in Antoine Griezmann's first season, has now been eliminated from playoff contention.

"We are very disappointed because we wanted to bring happiness to our fans, to our families, and everyone here at the stadium, and we couldn't," said Perelman. "That is frustrating for us, but at the same time, again, the effort was not enough, but it was there. This group of players will bring happiness and achievements to this club."

Cincinnati will now go on to face Nashville SC in the best-of-three round of the playoff series.

stories.headline: 'No one saw it coming': Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star
stories.summary: The Swans are notorious for bidding on draft night. But no one saw their heist of Lions Academy star Caylen Murray coming, given they didn't even meet his family. Jasper Chellappah looks into the fascinating happenings on night one of the AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Caylen Murray is the earliest pick to have his club-tied matching rights passed up in AFL Draft history. No one saw it coming, not even the Lions.

Make no mistake, this was a Sydney draft heist months in the making. The Swans ran the numbers and it showed Brisbane was three misly points short of matching a bid at pick 9. They pulled the trigger and watched on for five agonising minutes as trade partners disappeared one by one.

The three-time premiers were scrambling and the scenes unfolding inside their corporate box were increasingly uncomfortable. Each phone call was shorter than the last as candidates dried up in a race against time to find three points.

Up until that stage Sydney had not shown serious interest in Murray. They surely wouldn't bid on him without any leaks of interest from their camp; they surely couldn't bid on him without meeting his family.

A smokescreen devised in pre-draft analysis and 12 months of assessing Murray's talents was pulled at the perfect time to rip him out of Queensland. They feigned disinterest and caught the Lions napping. No one saw it coming, not least Brisbane's war room.

'Bidney' has been up to these tricks before. They'd made 11 bids in 10 years prior to last night, including Brisbane's own prospect Sam Marshall. They nearly snared Adelaide's Max Michalanney with a similar ploy in 2022.

As the dust settles, it's clear to see the Lions were undone by new draft rules that they themselves necessitated.

In 2022 they used 34, 35, 38, 40, and 41 to match Will Ashcroft's bid at pick 2. In 2024 they used 40, 42, 43, and 46 to match Levi Ashcroft's bid at pick 5. In 2025 they used 22, 23, and 39 to match a bid at pick 6 for Dan Annable. They achieved similar results for first-round talents Jaspa Fletcher and Marshall.

Brisbane had played the system to perfection up until Thursday night. But new draft rules require clubs to find the points to match with a maximum of two draft picks. A new draft value index (DVI) inflated the worth of top 10 picks. And a new levy added a 20% tax to bids matched by grand finalists.

Brisbane was caught looking too far ahead by sliding pick 19 down to 24 and 34. The 1355-point value of pick 9 became 1626 points with the grand finalist loading. Brisbane's picks 24 and 25 were worth 1211 points and they could go into a maximum of 412 points deficit on their future first-rounder. Tallied up and they accounted for 1623 of the 1626 points required.

The AFL values that gap at 1/1000th of the worth of the 3000 points Dougie Cochrane was matched with.

Sydney pulled off a coup to rival footy's very best off-field drama in 2026.

Brisbane's shortcoming wasn't just to the Swans's benefit, either. Gustavo Teixeira landed in St Kilda's lap at pick 11, a genuine pick one chance throughout the season. The flow-on effect kept coming with Collingwood grabbing their top target in mad Pies fan Sam Gayfer. Without the bid being matched these clubs effectively moved up the draft order.

Murray's shock was plain to see as reality set in. But the star academy graduate quickly recovered to deliver an extremely mature interview.

"I didn't realise Sydney was that keen but [I'm] stoked to join the club. It's an amazing club, great players, great staff and I'm keen to explore Sydney.

"It was a bit of a shock at the start but now it's sunk in. I'm stoked to be a Swans player."

The classy and composed halfback looms as a natural replacement for departed All-Australian Nick Blakey.

stories.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
stories.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
stories.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013.

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

'Breaking Bad' nears its end as 'Roar' rules the charts

One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out.

Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars.

Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010.

Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4.

The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem.

WNBA, MLB teams were building championship legacies

The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs.

MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however.

BCS era coming to a close

College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least.

One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign.

Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

stories.headline: Kayla Harrison, Amanda Nunes reclaim leading roles in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Who do Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes replace in ESPN's P4P women's top 10?
stories.body:
Hello (again), Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes. Goodbye (for now), Valentina Shevchenko and Zhang Weili. The top of the ESPN women's MMA pound-for-pound rankings has a new look.

Harrison and Nunes, both of whom had been ineligible for the top 10 because of inactivity, returned over the weekend for a clash of elites at UFC 334. Harrison, defending her bantamweight championship for the first time after nearly a year and a half out of the cage while healing from surgery for herniated discs in her neck, scored a fourth-round submission of Nunes, who had been retired for nearly 3½ years. As a result, Harrison takes over the No. 1 ranking and Nunes, a former two-division champion and the consensus GOAT of women's MMA, is No. 2.

The former occupants of those spots, Shevchenko and Zhang, are newly ineligible for the rankings because it's been over a year since they have fought and they have nothing scheduled. Those two former champions drop out, and the rest of the women's top 10 remains the same.

In the men's rankings, UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane moves up one spot to No. 7 on the strength of his decision win over Josh Hokit in their title bout at UFC 334.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Nov. 18. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Kayla Harrison

UFC bantamweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 20-1

Last: W (Sub4) vs. Amanda Nunes, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Harrison stepped into the Octagon at UFC 334 already a reigning champion, but her submission win over Nunes was truly her crowning achievement. The backstory about their shared training gym history added drama to the buildup, but what mattered most about this matchup was that Harrison, who had voiced her goal to be the greatest ever in women's MMA, was facing the woman who has lived up to that standard. After choking out Nunes, what can Harrison do for an encore? Can any other woman in the sport give her a fight? Maybe it won't come to that. Harrison and Nunes both called for a rematch -- but at featherweight. That would lessen Harrison's burden in dealing with her toughest foe: the weigh-in scale.

2. Amanda Nunes

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-6

Last: L (Sub4) vs. Kayla Harrison, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Nunes' return from retirement did not go as she had hoped, but her failing was not so much about deteriorated physical abilities as it was about her ill-advised choice to venture too much into the grappling wheelhouse of Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist. If Nunes gets the rematch both women are calling for, but this time at 145 pounds, that would seem to be to the advantage of Harrison, the bigger woman. But a redo would give Nunes another opportunity to lean into her own prodigious strength as a striker.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 13-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Virna Jandiroba, Nov. 7

Next: TBA

If Suarez was still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Loopy Godínez. Then she went on to beat another fellow top-10 strawweight, Jandiroba, sending a message to the division that Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

8. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

9. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

10. Jasmine Jasudavicius

UFC flyweight

Record: 16-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Erin Blanchfield, Oct. 17

Next: TBA

Jasudavicius was rising in the 125-pound division until being knocked out by Manon Fiorot last year, halting a five-fight winning streak. But she got back up and won two in a row, most recently an impressive grappling performance against Blanchfield, to reassert herself as a contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Kayla Harrison; 2. Amanda Nunes; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Tatiana Suarez; 6. Cris Cyborg; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Manon Fiorot; 9. Dakota Ditcheva; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Nunes; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Jasmine Jasudavicius.

Andrew Davis: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Suarez; 10. Jasudavicius.

Dre Waters: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Nunes; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Joselyne Edwards.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Jasudavicius.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 29-4

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Movsar Evloev, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. He did just that by handing Evloev his first loss at UFC 333.

3. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 21-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career, then completing his trilogy with Dvalishvili with a successful title defense. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet.

4. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

5. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: Jan. 30 vs. Manel Kape

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

7. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 15-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Josh Hokit, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ made his first defense against Hokit at UFC 334, winning a slugfest.

8. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 7

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

9. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 21-6

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. Their third meeting at UFC 333 was the most competitive in their trilogy, but Dvalishvili fell short again.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: Dec. 12 vs. Sergei Pavlovich

Pereira made a big splash in the MMA after a world championship career in kickboxing. He joined the UFC in 2021 and became a middleweight champion the following year, then moved on to be a two-time light heavyweight titlist before making an unprecedented bid for a belt in a third weight class when he fought Game at UFC Freedom 250 for an interim heavyweight title. Pereira got knocked out in that fight, but now he's back on his feet and in position to reclaim his position when he faces a fellow title contender, Pavlovich, at UFC 335.

Other fighters receiving votes: Alexandre Pantoja and Sean Strickland.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Liverpool face Man United amid dismal record at Anfield, but will it matter?
stories.summary: Anfield has a power to propel Liverpool to the greatest heights, but the team are struggling for form there this season and rivals Manchester United are up next.
stories.body:
When Manchester United traveled to Anfield to face Jürgen Klopp's beleaguered Liverpool side in March 2023, former United captain Gary Neville was sure his old club would emerge triumphant. "I'm not nervous," he told Sky Sports. "I've never been more relaxed coming here in the last nine years as a Manchester United fan."

His conviction stemmed from the fact that United had only lost once in their last 13 Premier League games and had climbed up to third in the table under Erik ten Hag. Liverpool, meanwhile, were languishing in sixth and losing ground in the race for UEFA Champions League qualification.

The outcome of the game? Liverpool defied expectations by subjecting United to a 7-0 thrashing, the biggest win in the fixture's history. It was a powerful reminder that, regardless of form, Anfield at its best has an enduring power to propel Liverpool to the greatest heights.

However, in the three years since that memorable victory, Liverpool have failed in all three attempts to beat United when playing at home.

In December 2023, Klopp's side spurned the chance to go top of the table after their faltering archrivals held them to a 0-0 draw. The spoils were shared again the following season, when Amad Diallo netted late on in a 2-2 draw to end United's run of three straight defeats. And last term, Ruben Amorim's men went one better, beating Arne Slot's Premier League champions 2-1 to claim United's first win at Anfield in almost a decade.

On Sunday, Liverpool will host their old foe again in what will be a first taste of the fixture for both Andoni Iraola and new United manager Mauricio Pochettino. Struggling United are in the relegation zone (18th) and recently sacked Michael Carrick, so it is Liverpool, who are in the race for Europe (fourth), who should be confident. But their form at the iconic home stadium needs to change, and fast, if they are to spark their season into life.

Liverpool's dismal record at Anfield predates this season

United are not the only team to have enjoyed success at Anfield in recent times. This season, only bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace and 16th-place Nottingham Forest have picked up fewer points at home than Liverpool.

Iraola's side have won just one of their five Premier League games at Anfield, drawing and losing twice respectively -- the same home record as United.

That Liverpool have the best away record in the top flight this term -- winning four and drawing one of their five games on the road -- makes their struggles at Anfield all the more bewildering. Despite the stadium's reputation as one of the most feared venues in Europe for visiting teams, it is Liverpool's home form which is preventing them from establishing themselves as genuine title contenders this season.

There is some mitigation for the Reds' troubles at Anfield. Against both Manchester City and Arsenal, Iraola's side were on the receiving end of controversial refereeing decisions.

They collapsed against City after Ryan Gravenberch was contentiously sent off for two yellow-card offences, while the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel ruled Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for a shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 1-0 defeat to Arsenal. The KMI Panel also ruled in September that Forest should not have been awarded a penalty in the previous month's 2-2 draw at Anfield.

But while Liverpool can feel aggrieved about some of the decisions that have gone against them at home, it must also be acknowledged that their own performance levels have not been good enough. Against Arsenal, Iraola's side failed to have a single shot on target for the first time in 442 league matches at Anfield. In the 0-0 draw with Fulham in September, Liverpool were blunt and lethargic against a team that had yet to claim a single Premier League point.

That kind of insipid display was commonplace last season, when Liverpool failed to win 47% of their home games (winning just 10 out of 19). The underperformance of big-ticket signings such as Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak did not help matters, with fans often left wanting to see more from their new stars.

The increasing competitiveness of the Premier League -- where even teams towards the bottom of the table have the financial power to sign elite players -- means almost every game demands a certain level of performance. Too often over the past year, Liverpool have failed to reach that bar.

While it is impossible to pin down one definitive theory for the Reds' struggles, the events of the summer of 2025 -- when striker Diogo Jota and his brother André Silva lost their lives in a car accident -- cast a shadow over the whole campaign.

On an emotional level, there was debate about the supporters' decision to sing Jota's song at the 20-minute mark of every home match, and how much of an impact that had on his former teammates. More practically, the knock-on effect the tragedy had on Liverpool's pre-season preparations left several players struggling for fitness, particularly late on in games when the team needed a goal.

"It's difficult to pinpoint one overriding reason for why Liverpool's Anfield form in 2026 has been as indifferent as it has for at least a decade, but the origins perhaps trace back to the start of last season," Paul Gorst, Liverpool correspondent for the Liverpool Echo, told ESPN.

"Arne Slot took an undercooked, grieving squad of Premier League champions into the 2025-26 campaign after considerably rejigging the first team's makeup with several new players signed. As performances and results started to suffer from late September onwards, the noise on the Kop began to quieten down. Slot's brand of football quickly became one-paced and ordinary.

"A confidence-shot group of players, who by [former Liverpool defender] Andy Robertson's own admission, had no interest in football at that time, ran out of ideas and were unable to give the crowd the sort of jolt that launches them into action on the terraces."

Across the whole of 2026, Liverpool have won just five of their 15 league matches at Anfield, losing three. It is a far cry from the staggering run the Reds managed for a long spell under Klopp, who led his team to a club-record 68-game unbeaten home run in the league between April 2017 and January 2021.

Encompassed in that run was a sequence of 18 consecutive home victories -- a testament to what a fortress Anfield can be when Liverpool are operating at the peak of their powers -- but that feels a long way off right now.

'I think this atmosphere that we can create is special'
Cultivating an aura of invincibility at home does not happen overnight. After suffering his first defeat as Liverpool manager to Palace in November 2015, Klopp stressed the importance of the Anfield crowd in helping to change his team's fortunes.

"After the [Palace] goal on 82 minutes, with 12 minutes to go, I saw many people leaving the stadium," he said. "I felt pretty alone at this moment. We decide when it is over. Between 82 and 94 [minutes] you can make eight goals if you like."

Over the next nine years, supporters began to adopt that same mentality and they turned -- to coin one of Klopp's famous phrases -- from "doubters to believers." Now, Iraola and his team must try to take fans on a similar journey.

Last season, Liverpool felt the wrath of the home crowd on more than one occasion. It was a dismal campaign under Slot, who saw his credit in the bank as a title-winning coach dwindle as his side too often served up lifeless performances at Anfield.

For the very best teams, winning is an addictive habit. In a sport of such fine margins, even a subconscious acceptance of mediocrity can have a big impact.

"Last season, Fortress Anfield began to crumble and visiting teams became increasingly confident of getting a result," Gorst added. "All three promoted teams left with a point and its reputation as a fearsome venue for visiting teams took quite a hit."

Slot's Liverpool were regularly accused of being too slow and ponderous on the ball, with frustration from the stands palpable as the Reds struggled to break down stubborn defenses.

"To be honest, we need them behind us," Gravenberch told TNT Sports after Liverpool were booed off the pitch following a 1-1 draw with Chelsea in May. "Okay, we didn't win, but I don't really think we deserved this [reaction]. The fans have to be behind us for the full 90 minutes because when they were behind us in the second half, we were pressing really well. We need them. Hopefully they wouldn't do it again."

Gravenberch's comments pointed to the synergy that had been lost between what legendary former Liverpool boss Bill Shankly once described as "the holy trinity" of the players, manager and supporters. In the early months of this season -- despite a mixed bag of results -- there has been some evidence of that unity returning.

In the Champions League, Anfield has played a part in big Liverpool wins over Atlético Madrid (2-1) and Villarreal (4-3). Against the latter, the Reds came from 2-0 down to win a game in any competition for the first time in more than four years.

The Anfield atmosphere was also key in helping Liverpool get over the line in October's 2-0 win over Brighton & Hove Albion and in the Carabao Cup fourth-round tie with Chelsea a few days later.

"I think it's not just winning," Iraola said after those two victories. "I think, especially at Anfield, everyone feels when the team goes for it. When everyone is giving everything, when everyone is trying his best, our supporters will be there to help the team. Even when we first started losing in some of the last games, I think they've been there and they've helped us massively.

"The other day against Chelsea, I think the atmosphere was really, really good. It's nice to recover, to feel these things at home because we have a big advantage, with respect to other teams. I think this atmosphere that we can create is special."

Certainly, Iraola will hope the Anfield crowd can generate that kind of special atmosphere Sunday. United come into the game wounded, having failed to win any of their past eight league games -- their worst stretch in Premier League history.

However, Liverpool's surprise triumph in 2023 serves as a reminder that the form book does not always matter in fixtures of this magnitude.

Iraola and several of his players are still waiting for their first big Anfield moment. There would be no better time for them to have one than against Liverpool's most bitter rivals this weekend.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

With the World Series behind us, players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7 to Dec. 9.

However, as the current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, the 2027 season (as well as the financial rules that will govern it), players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Jump to:

Catcher | First base | Second base | Shortstop | Third base

Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Paul Goldschmidt, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base
Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop
Some free agents: Ha-Seong Kim, J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners
Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Some free agents: Alec Bohm, Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted), Teruaki Sato (posted)

Outfield
Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter
Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher
Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign SP Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Tarik Skubal, Michael King, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Freddy Peralta, Trevor Rogers (Q), Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to RHP Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Kaima Taira (posted), Hiromi Itoh (posted)
